talk_track: Daniel Kirichanski — I ran platform engineering at PayPal and Ripple, and my whole practice is the moment a scaling company's infrastructure and its leadership have to grow up at the same time. Overstory's Director of Platform Engineering posting says it plainly: 'we're evolving from early-stage infrastructure to a more mature, reliable platform that can support rapid product development and growing customer demand.' The same board is running a live Chief Technology Officer search. Read together, that means the platform transition — GCP, CI/CD, MLOps, reliability standards — is being architected while the seat that owns it sits empty. Whatever gets decided in that window is what the incoming CTO inherits, so the cheapest gift you can give your future hire is keeping those decisions reversible. Who owns the platform strategy until the CTO seat is filled?
